questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: At Queen Mary the courses are taught at an extremely high level by some of the world's top lawyers and attorneys, which is why in 2019 the Queen Mary School of Law was also ranked as the No. 32 best university in the world by QS World University Rankings. Queen Mary is also recognized as a culturally diverse university, even located in London; one of the most multicultural cities in the world. Overall, for an ambitious and curious student like me, this constitutes an ideal learning environment, as I thereby have the opportunity to live out my academic ambitions in a city with an abundance of culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything has been really good, however there was a lot of information that the administration was unsure about, e.g. when our exams were.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not the easiest, but not the most difficult either.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We did get a lot of info at the different info events. However, some information was really difficult to get.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite easy - I used a website called 'Open rent'.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is amazing. You get to live a more 'local' life living off campus. Also - the area around campus is not very nice. Thus, you get an option to live in nicer areas. However, as a lot of people are living on campus, a lot of associate student events are on campus.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite straight forward

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They send me an e-mail with the info they required in order to register at them, and then I sent them the info

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student administration - quick replies on e-mail

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull. I wanted to change courses, which was done without any problems.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: they made the process really easy

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not a lot of different courses to chose from, AND as a master student I could still only choose undergrad. courses. However, the teaching in the few courses was really good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I could only take undergrad. courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more reading, and not so much physical teaching. Might have had something to do with Covid though.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
- Comparative Constitutional Law
- Contract Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Contract Law and Competition Law

questions.answer: All events when going out costs between 5-20 pounds (going to bars etc.).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were cheaper than I expected. Going out was more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: London is the city of opportunities. It is so much fun. Pubs and bars close quite early though.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many many different ones. I did not stay at campus, so I joined a gym near my flat. A lot of the social and cultural events were organized by the associate students themselves.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Art exhibitions, museums, dining out, going out, going to the parks.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The countryside e.g.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Culture wise it is very similar to DK, and I had a lot of friends in London. So it was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be outgoing and social

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The humour

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- attend classes and read
- socialize with your co-students
- enjoy yourself

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: start applying for scholarships as early as possible. London is very expensive.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends for life

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: getting used to having classes and read academic material in English.
